# Moho compatibility patches to Luau

Vendored from crates.io `luau0-src 0.12.3+luau663`. To upgrade: copy the new
crate version here and re-apply the patches below (grep `RTS-CORE-ENGINE`).

| File | Change | Why |
|------|--------|-----|
| `luau/VM/src/lgc.cpp`, `lstate.h` (`RTS-CORE-ENGINE DETERMINISM`) | `luaC_step` runs a triggered cycle to completion (stop-the-world) instead of incremental steps, and `getheaptrigger` paces cycles on bytes instead of upstream's `lua_clock` allocation rate | GC timing is visible to scripts: weak tables (FAF's reclaim grid, TrashBags) and dead keys (a removed-then-re-added key lands elsewhere, changing `pairs` order). Wall-clock pacing, and incremental marking whose progress depends on table node order (light userdata keys still hash by address), made two runs of one game diverge. A whole cycle at a byte trigger depends only on reachability. Cost: a 40–60 ms pause on a 140–180 MB sim heap about every 25 game-seconds (inside the 100 ms tick budget; average tick cost unchanged) |
| `luau/VM/src/lgc.cpp`, `lstate.h`, `lstate.cpp`, `lgcdebug.cpp` (`RTS-CORE-ENGINE EPHEMERON`); `src/lib.rs` (`RTS_LUAU_HARDMEMTESTS`) | A table weak on one side keeps an entry's strong side alive only while its weak side is alive: a weak-keyed table's value while its key is (ephemerons, as Lua 5.2+), a weak-valued table's key while its value is. Undecided tables go on `g->ephemeron`; `convergeephemerons` (atomic phase) repeats over them until a pass marks nothing, then `cleartable` clears as before, and marks a string only if its entry stays. `RTS_LUAU_HARDMEMTESTS=1` builds the VM with its asserts and `luaC_validate` at every collection | Upstream marks the strong side of every entry, so a row of FAF's category cache (`cache[a][b]`, weak keys holding weak-valued rows, FAF 3841) outlived its dead key by one collection, and a temporary operand outlived its dead result by one. A collection tick's heap then held dead objects that a keyframe saved and a load's collection dropped (`tests/keyframes.rs`). Now a second collection frees nothing. Seen by scripts only through `pairs` on such a table: an entry whose strong side is reachable only through its own weak side (a value that references its key) is collected, where stock Lua, and moho's 5.0, keep it for as long as the table lives. Pause unchanged (22 ms on a 180 MB heap). Tests: `tests/lua_ephemerons.rs` |
| `luau/VM/src/lobject.h`, `lstate.h`, `lstate.cpp`, `ltable.cpp`, `lfunc.cpp`, `ludata.cpp`, `lbuffer.cpp`, `lmem.cpp` (`RTS-CORE-ENGINE DETERMINISM`) | Tables, userdata, buffers, closures and threads carry a 32-bit creation-order `gcid`; `ltable.cpp` hashes those keys by it instead of by address | Address hashing makes `pairs` order over table/object keys depend on the allocator and ASLR, so it differs between runs and machines |
| `luau/VM/src/laux.cpp`, `lapi.cpp`, `include/lua.h` (`RTS-CORE-ENGINE DETERMINISM`) | `tostring` of a table / function / userdata / thread / buffer prints its `gcid` (new `lua_gcid`) instead of the encoded address | FAF builds keys and log strings from `tostring(obj)`; address-based text differs between runs, changing string hash order and allocation (GC timing) |
| `luau/Common/include/Luau/DetMath.h` (new), `VM/src/lmathlib.cpp`, `lbuiltins.cpp`, `lveclib.cpp`, `lvmexecute.cpp`, `lnumutils.h`, `Compiler/src/BuiltinFolding.cpp`, `ConstantFolding.cpp` (`RTS-CORE-ENGINE DETERMINISM`) | `sin/cos/tan/asin/acos/atan/atan2/sinh/cosh/tanh/exp/log/log2/log10/pow` call `rts_det_*`, implemented in Rust (`src/engine/lua/det_math.rs`, the `libm` crate) and resolved at link time | The platform libm (Apple vs MSVC CRT) rounds some results differently: a Mac and a Windows peer desynced at tick 22006 of a 4v4 |
| `luau/VM/src/lapi.cpp`, `include/lua.h` (`RTS-CORE-ENGINE DEBUGNAME`) | New `lua_setcdebugname`: names an existing C function, as `lua_pushcclosurek`'s `debugname` does | mlua creates native callbacks unnamed, so a native method's argument error read `[C]: in ?`. The engine names each registered function (`Unit:SetBuildRate`, `src/lua_api`) so tracebacks, `debug.info` and the error explanations say which. Debug info only: no effect on the sim |
| `luau/VM/src/lsnapshot.cpp` (new), `lobject.h`, `lstate.h`, `lstate.cpp`, `lfunc.cpp`, `lapi.cpp` (`RTS-CORE-ENGINE SNAPSHOT`) | Saves a VM's heap (tables with their node layout, closures, suspended coroutines, upvalues, protos, strings) and loads it into a VM of the same build started up to the same base (`docs/architecture/replays.md`); `lua_snapshot_validate` checks every reference in a heap. Protos carry a creation-order `protoid` (like `gcid`) so a snapshot can name one the loading VM made itself. Userdata made with mlua's error-object destructor (`rts_internaldtor`, noted by the engine at start-up) take no gcid | Replay keyframes and save games (issue #363). mlua draws a pooled error object for every native call and makes a new one when calls nest deeper than before or an error uses one up: that history isn't in a keyframe, so those objects must not move the gcid counter. Otherwise additive |
| `luau/VM/src/ldebug.cpp`, `include/lua.h`, `lvmexecute.cpp` (`RTS-CORE-ENGINE DEBUGGER`) | New `lua_breakpointclosure`: `lua_breakpoint` for a closure pointer instead of a stack slot. In `LOP_BREAK`, when the `debugbreak` hook turns `singlestep` on, the rest of the call runs in the single-step interpreter (`luau_execute<true>` with a `resumeop` to start at the patched-out opcode) | The engine's Lua debugger (`src/engine/lua/debugger/`, `--lua-debug`): it sets breakpoints from the interrupt, without pushing a value or making an object in the sim VM. Upstream only reads `singlestep` when the interpreter is entered, so a step from a breakpoint ran on to the end of the call. Without a debugger attached nothing calls either |
| `src/lib.rs` (the build) | `-ffp-contract=off` (`/fp:precise` on MSVC) | Apple clang fused multiply-adds (205 in the VM: Lua `%`, `math.lerp`), x86 MSVC doesn't: different rounding |
| `luau/VM/src/lvmutils.cpp` | `luaV_lessthan` / `luaV_lessequal` order mismatched operand types by type tag (nil < boolean < number < string < table ...), as the exe's `luaV_lessthan` (0x994c90) does; same-type unordered values still raise | Moho's Lua 5.0 does not raise on `nil < x` / `false > 0`; FAF needs `nil > 80` false (blueprint post-processing), `false > 0` false, and `number > nil` true (`GetTopmostWorldViewAt`) |

The comparison patch only touches slow paths (number/number comparisons never
reach it). The `gcid` costs 4 bytes per object header (lmem.cpp asserts).

When patching another C++ file, add it to `_MOHO_PATCHED_SOURCES` in
`src/lib.rs` — Cargo only fingerprints Rust sources, so without that the
change won't trigger a rebuild.
